name: Combinatorial Eluder Dimension / Radon Number (affine)
details: For every finite binary concept class, $\mathrm{Edim}(\mathcal H)\geq\mathrm{Rad}(\mathcal H)-1$.
proof: Let $R=\{h_1,\ldots,h_r\}$ be Radon independent and take $h_r$ as the base hypothesis.  As in the singleton-versus-rest argument, for every $i<r$ there is a coordinate $x_i$ on which $h_i$ differs from every member of $R\setminus\{h_i\}$.  The coordinates are distinct when $r\geq3$.  Order the pairs $(x_i,h_i)$ for $i=1,\ldots,r-1$.  At $x_i$, $h_i$ differs from the base $h_r$, while for every $j<i$, both $h_i$ and $h_r$ are among the members other than $h_j$ and hence agree at $x_j$.  These pairs form an eluder sequence of length $r-1$.  The cases $r\leq2$ follow directly from the definitions.
witness_verification: For the full cube, combinatorial eluder dimension is $n$ while the Radon number is $\lfloor\log_2(2n+2)\rfloor$, so no reverse affine-linear bound holds.
